topics.title: Defining psychology: mental processes, experience and behaviour

concepts.learning_objective: Students will state the formal definition of psychology and the origin of the term.
Students will distinguish mental processes from brain activity and explain why experiences are subjective.
Students will classify behaviours as overt or covert and relate them to stimulus and response.

topics.title: Psychology as a discipline: natural science and social science
topics.ncert_sections: Psychology as a Discipline; Psychology as a Natural Science; Psychology as a Social Science

concepts.learning_objective: Students will explain how the hypothetico-deductive model guides psychology as a natural science.
Students will explain how psychology studies individuals in their socio-cultural context.
Students will explain why the mind is considered distinct from, though dependent on, the brain.
Students will describe evidence from affective neuroscience that the mind influences bodily processes.

topics.title: Popular notions about psychology
topics.ncert_sections: Popular Notions about the Discipline of Psychology

concepts.learning_objective: Students will explain why common-sense explanations of behaviour rely on hindsight.
Students will interpret Dweck's study as an example of scientific findings that run against common sense.
Students will compare Wundt's structuralism with James's functionalism.
Students will describe Gestalt psychology and behaviourism as reactions to structuralism.
Students will distinguish psychoanalytic, humanistic, cognitive and constructivist perspectives.
Students will identify the landmarks of the modern era of psychology in India.
Students will sequence Durganand Sinha's four phases of psychology in India.
Students will match problems to the appropriate branch of psychology.
Students will distinguish a clinical psychologist from a psychiatrist.

topics.title: Psychology, other disciplines and everyday life
topics.ncert_sections: Psychology and Other Disciplines; Psychology in Everyday Life

concepts.learning_objective: Students will explain how psychology contributes to and draws from other disciplines.
Students will apply psychological understanding to personal and social problems in daily life.
